items.description: Checks are due to start in October, and the administration has not said how it arrived at $500 or which years the disputed fees cover.

items.title: Physicians who survive life-threatening illness often clash with their own patient identity
items.description: A JAMA Network Open qualitative study of 22 physicians finds leave policies and leadership sensitivity shape whether doctors successfully return to clinical practice after serious illness

items.title: The hidden data problem costing physicians time, referrals and patients
items.description: New national research shows health systems and health plans still can't get provider data right — and the fallout lands squarely on physician practices

items.title: Sen. Roger Marshall's obstetrics practice sued more than 700 patients over unpaid bills
items.description: Kansas court records reviewed by The New York Times show the practice charged 18% annual interest, garnished bank accounts and pursued arrest warrants over balances as small as $101.

items.title: Bipartisan Senate bill would send $10 billion to primary care and rework how Medicare values physician work
items.description: The Pay PCPs Act of 2026 would blend prospective per-patient payments with fee-for-service, halve beneficiary cost sharing for primary care and exempt participating physicians from MIPS.

items.title: Virtual kidney-care companies show no consistent benefit despite billions in investment, PHTI finds
items.description: A review of eight leading virtual chronic kidney disease management solutions found minimal cost savings and no clear evidence of slowed disease progression, according to the Peterson Health Technology Institute.

items.title: Nurses need a seat at the table in developing AI strategy
items.description: Health systems need to get nurses involved in choosing, designing and deploying AI solutions at the outset.

items.title: The case for continuous intelligence in healthcare operations | Viewpoint
items.description: The goal is not to replace strategic optimization projects, but to extend their value by monitoring how real operations are changing.

items.title: Peggy Lillis Foundation Will Honor C diff Advocates at Annual Gala
items.description: The Peggy Lillis Foundation will host its 17th Annual Changing the Odds Gala this month in New York City, and it will include a casino, fellowship amongst the C diff community, and an award ceremony honoring a physician-scientist, philanthropist, a researcher, and a patient advocate for their contributions to C difficile awareness, treatment, and prevention.

items.title: REMAP-CAP and the Tamiflu “Pre-Release”: A Set-Up for Disaster
items.description: Preliminary REMAP-CAP data suggesting oseltamivir may increase mortality in critically ill ICU influenza patients has sparked polarized reactions, but clinicians should await the full peer-reviewed manuscript before drawing broad conclusions, since the signal comes from a narrow, severely ill population and may reflect a therapeutic window effect rather than a blanket lack of efficacy.

items.title: Measles Resurgence Exposes US Vaccine Policy Risks, Experts Warn
items.description: Jesse Goodman, MD, MPH, provides nuance regarding HHS’ suggestion to separate MMR combination vaccines as well as the looming elimination status review in November.

items.title: Study Identifies Patients at Risk for Severe COVID-19 Post-Vaccination
items.description: A population-level analysis finds that age, comorbidity burden, and long-term care residence continue to drive severe outcomes.

items.title: John Sfakianos, MD, discusses evolving management of recurrent LG-IR-NMIBC
items.description: John P. Sfakianos, MD, discusses the challenges of managing recurrent LG-IR-NMIBC and the role of chemoablation.

items.title: App-based intervention aims to increase PSA screening among Black men
items.description: A randomized trial will test whether an app-guided, at-home PSA screening approach can improve prostate cancer screening among Black men.

items.title: Dabogratinib shows early activity in FGFR3-altered LG-IR-NMIBC
items.description: Dabogratinib showed early activity and manageable safety in FGFR3-altered LG-IR-NMIBC, supporting advancement to a planned registrational study in the adjuvant setting.

items.title: The critical role of advocacy in urologic oncology
items.description: Advocacy through groups like BCAN and the AUA shapes urologic oncology policy���driving funding, screening access, and equity in cancer care, the authors write.

items.description: Can you guess the diagnosis?

items.title: Vosoritide improves growth velocity in children with hypochondroplasia, phase 3 trial shows
items.description: Phase 3 CANOPY-HCH-3 data show vosoritide significantly improved growth velocity, height, and arm span in children with hypochondroplasia.

items.title: CDC-backed surveillance finds 4 in 5 child deaths preventable across 7 high-mortality countries
items.description: A CDC-backed CHAMPS surveillance report across 7 countries finds 80% of child deaths were preventable, with gram-negative bacteria driving neonatal sepsis.

items.title: 5 Shifts Redefining Automation
items.description: Automation is reshaping patient access and financial clearance. But when tools are disconnected, they can create fragmented workflows, delayed decisions and added staff burden.Our new e-book explores five shifts that can help health systems move beyond point solutions and build a more connected pre-care automation strategy. You’ll learn how real-time insight, strategic workflows and human expertise can help simplify access, reduce rework and support stronger financial performance.

items.title: Changes: Brad Goettl, American Nurses Enterprise, on AI and nursing
items.description: In a new episode of our video series, we discuss a partnership with the Johnson & Johnson Foundation and Google to boost AI skills in the nursing workforce.

items.title: The leadership advantage hospitals can't afford to ignore | Viewpoint
items.description: In many industries, organizations build credibility by showing efficiency with resources before asking for more. Healthcare should be no exception.

items.title: From Pathogen to Infectious Disease Diagnosis: Rapid Genotyping Could Bring Ciprofloxacin Back for Gonorrhea Cases
items.description: Resistance-guided testing targeting a single gene mutation could let clinicians safely reintroduce ciprofloxacin for the majority of gonorrhea cases still susceptible to it, sparing ceftriaxone as resistance climbs worldwide. Lao-Tzu Allan-Blitz, MD, MPH, offers insights into his work in this area.

items.title: Ixekizumab, Tirzepatide Maintains Efficacy in Psoriatic Disease
items.description: The combination outperformed ixekizumab alone on skin, joint, and weight outcomes through 52 weeks.

items.title: Wicked Good Cardiometabolic Chat: Once-Weekly Insulin Management
items.description: Once-weekly basal insulin has moved from an intriguing possibility to a new clinical reality.

items.title: Vaccine Messaging That Resonates With Hesitant Pharmacy Patients
items.description: Personalizing risk, offering a platform alternative, and timing the appointment around a patient's weekend can turn a hesitant conversation into a completed COVID-19 vaccination.

items.title: How mRNA and Protein-Based COVID-19 Vaccines Work
items.description: mRNA and protein-based COVID-19 vaccines reach the same immune target through different biological routes, a distinction pharmacists can use to guide product selection for patients.

items.title: Declining MMR Rates Rely on Collaboration for Path Forward
items.description: Molly O’Shea, MD, FAAP, shares insights on MMR coverage, measles outbreaks, and the pharmacist’s role from the perspective of a pediatrician.

items.title: Zepbound Lowers Health Care Costs in Older Adults With Obesity
items.description: Data shows that those who stayed on tirzepatide had monthly health care costs well below those of untreated adults.

items.title: First commercial procedures performed with Zenflow Spring for BPH
items.description: The Zenflow Spring Implant and Delivery System has entered commercial use for BPH following its FDA approval in December 2025.

items.title: AI-generated profiles impersonate female urologists to market ED products online
items.description: Scammers are stealing female urologists' headshots to run AI-driven catfishing and supplement scams; in this article, 2 urologists share their experiences with this concerning trend.

items.title: TRT, GLP-1s, and peptides: How to counsel patients stacking longevity therapies
items.description: Rising patient interest in TRT, GLP-1s, and peptide stacking requires clinicians to anchor conversations in evidence tiers, use baseline DEXA scans to monitor body composition, and engage patient goals without endorsing unsupported claims.

items.title: Semaglutide improves BMI category in children aged 6 to 11 years in phase 3 trial
items.description: Semaglutide plus lifestyle changes moved 40.4% of children below the obesity threshold at 68 weeks in the phase 3 STEP Young trial.

items.title: ARTEMIS trial data show Bifidobacterium-HMO synbiotic is safe and colonizes the infant, toddler gut
items.description: Persephone's ARTEMIS trial found its Bifidobacterium-HMO synbiotic safe and effective at gut colonization in 114 infants and toddlers.

items.description: Can you guess the diagnosis?

items.description: Sr. Mary Haddad talks with us about Medicaid cuts, more uninsured patients and the financial toll on hospitals.

items.title: ChristianaCare’s new CEO takes the post: MED MOVES
items.description: Kaiser Permanente names a leader in its Colorado market.

items.title: Who will define healthcare's AI standards? An executive order fuels the conversation | Viewpoint
items.description: The risk comes in how AI is deployed inside and across the healthcare system.

items.title: The Latest in Food: Updates on Outbreaks to Federal Policies Affecting Food Safety
items.description: Here's the latest on the cyclosporiasis and jalapeño-linked Salmonella case numbers, plus an update on the resolved avocado inspection halt. Also included is information on a bacterial infection linked to shellfish, and a look at efforts affecting cyclosporiasis research.

items.title: Pharmacy Technician Shines Light on Expanding Role
items.description: Pharmacy technician, Sharon Lucas, showcases how community pharmacy, clinical skills, and lifelong learning are transforming patient care.

items.title: Higher saturated fat intake associated with increased mortality in nonmetastatic prostate cancer
items.description: Higher saturated and animal fat intake was linked to increased mortality among men with nonmetastatic prostate cancer, according to a cohort study published in JAMA Network Open.

items.title: Contemporary Pediatrics week in review: August 31-September 4, 2026
items.description: Review some of the top stories from the Contemporary Pediatrics website over the last week, and catch up on anything you may have missed.

items.title: What to expect in the August/September 2026 issue of Contemporary Pediatrics
items.description: Get back-to-school pediatric guidance on vaccine updates, infection FAQs, screen time and mental health, nutrition changes, and standout cases to watch this year.

items.title: Abbott launches first ready-to-feed whole milk infant formula in the U.S.
items.description: Abbott launches Similac 360 Total Care Made With Whole Milk, the first commercially sterile, ready-to-feed liquid formula made with whole milk sold in the US, priced near its powdered line.

items.title: Bifidobacteria Decline: Causes and Consequences for Infant Gut Health
items.description: Infant-type bifidobacteria are considered keystone gut commensals — but newer data suggest they're becoming less common. Jarvinen-Seppo unpacks why, and what's driving the shift.

items.title: 2 Triples and a Dual Regimen Vie for First-Line Against H pylori
items.description: Adding bismuth to amoxicillin-vonoprazan increased efficacy of the combination for H pylori, and exceeded that of clarithromycin-based triple therapy without contributing to clarithromycin resistance.

items.title: From AIDS to COVID-19 to Measles, Why do Infectious Disease Public Health Crises Keep Occurring?
items.description: In the third episode of the series with Perry N. Halkitis, PhD, MS, MPH, he discusses how human behavior as well as other factors play a significant role in repeating outbreaks.

items.title: Drawing Borders Around a Borderless Specialty
items.description: Editor in chief Jason Gallagher, PharmD, FCCP, FIDP, FIDSA, BCPS, discusses the proposed OMB rule restricting federal grants for international research collaboration, and how it threatens infectious disease medicine's inherently borderless surveillance networks, publication access, and knowledge-sharing systems.

items.title: Referral Pathways and Unmet Needs in Perioperative MIBC Care
items.description: The data are compelling, but only if patients reach a medical oncologist. Joshua J. Meeks, MD, PhD, tackles the unresolved questions in MIBC care and lays out the referral steps every community urologist can take today.

items.title: MIBC Treatment Timeline and Skin Toxicity: What Urologists Should Know
items.description: With the recent FDA approval of enfortumab vedotin-ejfv (Padcev) plus pembrolizumab (Keytruda) in MIBC, Joshua J. Meeks, MD, PhD, maps the treatment timeline patients should expect and the skin reactions that warrant an urgent referral.

items.title: What the Efficacy Data from KEYNOTE-B15/EV-304 Revealed
items.description: For the first time in 25 years, a nonplatinum regimen beats cisplatin-based chemotherapy head-to-head. Joshua J. Meeks, MD, PhD, breaks down the KEYNOTE-B15/EV-304 data driving that shift.

items.title: FDA Expands MIBC Approval: What Changed for Platinum-Eligible Patients
items.description: A single FDA update just erased the platinum-eligibility line dividing patients with MIBC. Joshua J. Meeks, MD, PhD, explains what changed on July 10 and why a new subcutaneous option could ease access for rural patients

items.title: The UroOnc Minute: Perioperative Intravesical Chemotherapy at Nephroureterectomy, With Surena F. Matin, MD, FACS
items.description: In this episode, Surena F. Matin, MD, FACS, discusses the evidence and practical considerations surrounding perioperative intravesical chemotherapy to reduce bladder recurrence after nephroureterectomy.

items.title: FDA reports increased demand, supply efforts for estradiol transdermal patches
items.description: The FDA has provided an update on efforts to increase the supply of estradiol transdermal patches amid rising demand.

items.title: FDA news in pediatrics: August 2026
items.description: A recap of the top FDA approvals, authorizations, and regulatory decisions affecting pediatric care during August 2026.

items.title: The unharmonious 2026 child and adolescent immunization schedule - addendum
items.description: Five rapid developments — new mRNA flu vaccine, CDC director, ACIP/NVAC charters, a vaccine order, and an HHS RFI — roil the 2026 schedule.

items.title: The unharmonious 2026 child and adolescent immunization schedule
items.description: Court fight over CDC 2026 childhood vaccine schedule shifts shots to shared decision-making; experts warn lower uptake for Hep A, B, flu, COVID.

items.title: What can pediatricians learn from food depictions in children's books?
items.description: A content analysis of 159 picture books found food often symbolized family connection and culture more than nutrition alone, according to Carol Duh-Leong, MD, MPP.

items.title: Helping patients with well-founded mistrust in medicine
items.description: Amidst efforts to improve vaccinations and counter misinformation, doctors also must help those who have had bad experiences in health systems.

items.title: Making digital tools work for patients and doctors: Data Book podcast
items.description: Dr. Vanessa Diaz of MUSC Health talks about digital transformation in the latest episode of Data Book, a podcast from Chief Healthcare Executive.

items.title: Latest Vaccine and Immunization Efficacy, Safety for RSV, Influenza, and COVID-19
items.description: The Vaccine Integrity Project, in collaboration with the American Medical Association, conducted a vaccine and immunization effectiveness and safety review for RSV, Influenza, and COVID-19 for the 2026-2027 season. JAMA published the review, and here is an overview of the data going into this year's seasonal respiratory virus season.

items.title: New Olive Oil Recall, Update on Rice Recall
items.description: Kofinas Mediterranean olive oil was recalled over an unapproved garlic flavoring ingredient, and a new update on Lundberg Family Farms' jasmine rice recall tied to foreign material contamination.

items.title: FDA approves zilganersen (Zanvastro) as first treatment for Alexander disease
items.description: The FDA approved zilganersen (Zanvastro) for Alexander disease in patients from infancy through adulthood, based on Phase 1-3 gait speed data.

items.title: Evidence review supports respiratory virus immunizations for 2026-2027 season
items.description: New evidence supports influenza, COVID-19, and RSV immunizations for reducing severe respiratory illness and hospitalization.

items.title: HPV vaccination coverage stalls for fourth straight year as rural-urban gap persists, CDC finds
items.description: CDC's 2025 NIS-Teen data show HPV vaccine coverage flat for a fourth year, with rural adolescents 12 points behind urban peers in receiving ≥1 dose.

items.title: Expanding AI while ensuring patient safety
items.description: Health systems are accelerating clinical uses of AI, but leaders stress the need for safegauards.

items.title: Wellstar plans to acquire another Georgia hospital
items.description: The system and Stephens County Hospital have reached an agreement on a deal, the latest in a busy period for Wellstar.

items.title: Beyond Approval: Finding the Right Place for Emerging Gram-Negative Antibiotics
items.description: The expanding gram-negative antibiotic pipeline offers important new treatment options; however, FDA approval alone does not define a drug’s place in therapy. Clinicians must weigh the clinical problems that each agent solves, the strength of the evidence behind it, and what remains unknown before incorporating these therapies into routine practice.

items.title: Paxlovid Shows No Benefit for Long COVID
items.description: The antiviral did not produce greater symptom improvement than placebo in patients with the condition in the RECOVER-VITAL trial.

items.title: Doctors report spike in misinformation from patients
items.description: The Physicians Foundation says more doctors say misinformation is affecting their ability to provide care.

items.title: Sanford Health finalizes merger with North Memorial Health
items.description: The Minnesota system will become part of Sanford Health, and Sanford will invest $600 million in facility upgrades.

items.title: GSK's mRNA Influenza Vaccine Moves to Phase 3 Trial
items.description: GSK will advance its investigational mRNA seasonal flu vaccine candidate, which targets both hemagglutinin and neuraminidase, into a phase 3 trial in September 2026 after the shot outperformed licensed flu vaccines in a phase 2 study.

items.title: A Review of Vibrio vulnificus: Clinical Presentation and Treatment
items.description: Vibrio species are bacteria that live in saltwater environments. When ingested orally or through contact with open wounds, some species can cause severe life-threatening infections, particularly in those with high-risk conditions, such as liver disease. Here is a review of Vibrio vulnificus and the recommended antibiotic treatment.

items.title: Looking at the measles outbreak in Lancaster County, Pa.
items.description: More than 500 measles cases have been reported in the county this year.

items.title: Dealing with measles: Lessons from Pennsylvania
items.description: Doctors talk about the steps they’re taking and offer advice for hospitals.

items.title: 2026 FDA Approvals: Infectious Disease Vaccines
items.description: Here is a comprehensive list of vaccines approved this year as well as background information on the clinical data for each of them.

items.title: Patients With Infective Endocarditis Survived Longer with Shorter Period of Antibiotic Treatment
items.description: A shortened, response-tailored antibiotic treatment of infective endocarditis was associated with longer survival, but higher incidence of relapse.

items.title: Chief Healthcare Executive Roundtable: Reasons for hope
items.description: In the final segment from our panel discussion, executives explain where they are upbeat even in a time of change and turmoil.

items.title: Azithromycin in ER Did Not Reduce Wheezing in Preschoolers
items.description: Although azithromycin or another antibiotic is given to an estimated one of four preschool-age children in emergency departments for wheezing episodes, it failed to demonstrate benefit in a new multi-center trial.

items.title: As People With HIV Age, Who Is the Best Medical Provider for Them?
items.description: In the second episode of the series with Perry N. Halkitis, PhD, MS, MPH, he brings his personal experience to this topic and questions whether there should be a shift in who manages the primary care needs of these patients.

items.title: FDA Approves Gilead's Bixlenvo, Smallest Once-Daily Single Tablet Regimen for HIV
items.description: The federal agency gave the nod for the smallest once-daily single tablet regimen available for virologically suppressed adults with HIV, including those on complex regimens. The approval is based on the results of the 2 phase 3 ARTISTRY trials.

items.title: FDA Approves Multiple COVID-19 Vaccines With Protection Against XFG variant
items.description: The FDA has approved formulations for the 2026-2027 vaccines including Pfizer-BioNTech's Comirnaty XFG, Novavax's commercial partners Sanofi and Takeda have secured approvals for its Nuvaxovid, and Moderna's Spikevax and mNEXSPIKE vaccines, all with protections against the currently circulating variant.
